identity.title: Systolic BP <90 mmHg (or MAP <65) at the bedside

technique.how: Measure with a correctly sized cuff on a supported arm (manual if the automated reading is doubtful or the pulse is irregular), repeat, and measure both arms when dissection is possible; calculate MAP = (SBP + 2 x DBP)/3. Interpret against the patient's usual pressure and drug list.
technique.prerequisites: Appropriate cuff size; awareness of baseline BP, beta-blockers/antihypertensives and pacing.
technique.contraindications: Avoid the arm with a dialysis fistula, lymphoedema or recent axillary surgery; none otherwise.

interpretation.positive_finding: SBP <90 (or MAP <65) is shock until proven otherwise and should trigger a search for the cause (septic, hypovolaemic/haemorrhagic, cardiogenic, obstructive: tamponade/PE/tension pneumothorax, anaphylaxis, adrenal). In suspected dissection, hypotension roughly triples the odds (LR+ 2.9, specificity 95%). It is not a discriminator between causes.
interpretation.negative_finding: A normal SBP does not exclude shock (compensated haemorrhage, early sepsis, cardiogenic shock with vasoconstriction) or tamponade (about 60% of tamponade patients had SBP ≥100), nor low cardiac index in heart failure (SBP <90 sensitivity 12%).
interpretation.pitfalls: Chronic hypertensives are hypoperfused at 'normal' pressures; beta-blockers, pacemakers and automated cuffs in AF mislead. Interarm difference >20 mmHg raises dissection concern. Cuff readings overestimate true pressure in profound vasoconstriction.
interpretation.changes_what: SBP <90/MAP <65: resuscitate, lactate, POCUS (RUSH) to classify shock type, cause-directed therapy now. Normal BP: keep looking for compensated shock (HR, lactate, mentation, urine output).

estimates.target_condition: Acute aortic dissection; finding = hypotension as defined by each primary study (thresholds varied; not uniformly SBP <90 mmHg)
estimates.population: Pooled 4 studies of ED patients evaluated for suspected acute aortic dissection (review total 9 studies, 2,400 participants; prevalence range 21.9-76.1%)
estimates.reference_standard: Acute aortic dissection confirmed by imaging, surgery or autopsy per primary studies

estimates.target_condition: Low cardiac index <2.3 L/min/m2 in advanced heart failure; finding = SBP <90 mmHg on baseline examination
estimates.population: 188 patients hospitalised with advanced decompensated HF in the ESCAPE trial with pulmonary artery catheter measurements
estimates.reference_standard: Invasively measured cardiac index <2.3 L/min/m2 by pulmonary artery catheter
estimates.computed_from: Table 5 prints sensitivity 12%, specificity 84%, LR+ 0.77 and 'negative LR 0.96' (reciprocal form: 0.84/0.88 = 0.955). Conventional LR- = (1-0.12)/0.84 = 1.05 entered. LR+ <1 means SBP <90 did not identify low cardiac index in this population.
estimates.location: Table 5 (Utility of history and physical examination in detecting an invasively measured cardiac index <2.3 L/min/m2); columns frequency, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, LR+, LR-, OR, P

estimates.target_condition: Cardiac tamponade (sensitivity only); finding = systolic BP <100 mmHg (threshold differs from id title's <90)
estimates.population: 56 medical patients with cardiac tamponade, single-centre case series, University of Cincinnati
estimates.reference_standard: Clinical/haemodynamic diagnosis of tamponade with relief by pericardiocentesis or pericardial resection
estimates.computed_from: SBP ≥100 mmHg in 35 patients; assuming the full series denominator of 56, SBP <100 in 21/56 = 0.375. The abstract does not state how many had BP recorded, so the denominator is an assumption.
estimates.quote: heart sounds were diminished in 19 patients; arterial systolic pressure was greater than or equal to 100 mm Hg in 35

sources.citation: Ohle R, Kareemi HK, Wells G, Perry JJ. Clinical examination for acute aortic dissection: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Acad Emerg Med. 2019.

Drazner MH, Hellkamp AS, Leier CV, Shah MR, Miller LW, Russell SD, Young JB, Califf RM, et al. Value of clinician assessment of hemodynamics in advanced heart failure: the ESCAPE trial. Circ Heart Fail. 2009.
Guberman BA, Fowler NO, Engel PJ, Gueron M, Allen JM. Cardiac tamponade in medical patients. Circulation. 1981.
Roy CL, Minor MA, Brookhart MA, Choudhry NK. Does this patient with a pericardial effusion have cardiac tamponade? JAMA. 2007.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use a single normal cuff reading to exclude shock or tamponade; do not interpret SBP <90 as 'baseline' without documented prior values.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: SBP <90 or MAP <65 with altered mentation, lactate >2, oliguria or cool skin is shock: immediate resuscitation and senior/ICU review; in suspected dissection or tamponade, hypotension signals imminent collapse.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Automated versus manual cuff readings differ, particularly in arrhythmia and vasoconstriction; no kappa located.

extraction_notes: Hypotension is a severity marker across many diagnoses, so only accuracy data anchored to a specific target were entered, each with its own threshold stated. (1) Ohle 2019: pooled specificity 95% and LR+ 2.9 (1.8-4.6) for dissection; the abstract does not give the hypotension threshold or sensitivity, and prevalence is a range (21.9-76.1%), so left null. (2) ESCAPE Table 5 (PMC full text) gives an SBP <90 row for cardiac index <2.3: sens 12%, spec 84%, LR+ 0.77 — note direction: in advanced HF inpatients hypotension did NOT identify low output (OR 0.74, 95% CI 0.30-1.83, P = 0.5); Table 5's LR- column is in reciprocal form, so LR- was recomputed (computed=true). SBP <100 in the same table: sens 42%, spec 66%, LR+ 1.24 (Table 5). (3) Guberman 1981 tamponade series: sensitivity only, threshold <100, denominator assumed. Roy 2007 RCE (PMID 17456823) is not in PMC and its abstract does not report hypotension, so its pooled tamponade hypotension sensitivity could not be quoted (unverified recall: ~26%). No source for MAP <65 as a diagnostic discriminator was located; it is a sepsis/shock definitional threshold (Sepsis-3, unverified recall).
